answer: A nebula of cheap identities collapses when each agent must stake a bond that only unlocks after its work is graded over a long horizon: creating ten thousand sock puppets means locking ten thousand bonds, and a single detected forgery slashes the whole cluster. An atlas of public, signed reputation records then lets any counterparty check whether an identity has actually earned trust, so new Sybils start at zero and cannot buy history. The attack stops paying once identities cost more to forge than the rewards they can extract.
